subject: general
question: Which of the following correctly identifies an element that DOES NOT exist as a molecule in nature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium** is a noble gas and exists as a **monoatomic element** in nature, not as a molecule. This is because noble gases have a complete outer electron shell, making them highly stable and unreactive.
 
• Unlike elements such as **Chlorine (Cl₂)**, **Hydrogen (H₂)**, and **Iodine (I₂)**, which form diatomic molecules in their natural state due to their need to achieve stability through covalent bonding, helium does not need to bond with other atoms.
 
• Chlorine, hydrogen, and iodine naturally form diatomic molecules because their atoms share electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration (the octet rule).
 
• Helium is part of Group 18 (the noble gases) in the periodic table and has only two electrons in its outer shell, which is the maximum capacity for the first energy level. This makes it inherently stable.
 
• Helium's inertness and stability are why it exists as single atoms in nature, unlike other elements listed in the question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Noble Gases:**

 
 
• The noble gases include **helium (He)**, **neon (Ne)**, **argon (Ar)**, **krypton (Kr)**, **xenon (Xe)**, and **radon (Rn)**.
 
• They are characterized by their **complete valence electron shells**, which make them chemically inert and highly stable under normal conditions.
 
• Noble gases are often used in applications where reactivity needs to be minimized, such as helium in balloons or neon in lighting.
 
 
 
• **Diatomic Molecules:**
 
 
• Elements like **hydrogen (H₂)**, **chlorine (Cl₂)**, and **iodine (I₂)** naturally exist as diatomic molecules because they share electrons through covalent bonds to achieve a stable electronic configuration.
 
• The diatomic nature of these molecules ensures their stability and is a common feature among nonmetals in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Helium's Applications:**
 
 
• Helium is widely used in **cryogenics**, particularly in the cooling of superconducting magnets.
 
• It is also used in **scientific research** as an inert atmosphere for experiments and as a carrier gas in gas chromatography.
 
• Helium’s low density and non-flammable nature make it ideal for filling balloons and airships.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Grouping:**
 
 
• The periodic table groups elements based on their chemical properties, and noble gases are placed in Group 18 due to their **inert nature**.
 
• In contrast, elements like chlorine and iodine belong to the halogens in Group 17, characterized by their high reactivity and tendency to form diatomic molecules.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monoatomic vs. Diatomic Elements:**

 
 
• **Monoatomic:** Helium and other noble gases naturally exist as single atoms due to their stability.
 
• **Diatomic:** Nonmetal elements like hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine, and iodine form diatomic molecules to achieve stability through covalent bonding.
 
 
 
• **Helium Discovery:**
 
 
• Helium was first discovered in the **sun's spectrum** during a solar eclipse in **1868** by French astronomer **Jules Janssen** and English astronomer **Norman Lockyer**.
 
• The element is named after the Greek word **“Helios”**, meaning the sun.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity of Noble Gases:**
 
 
• Noble gases are generally unreactive due to their complete electron shells, but under extreme conditions, some (like xenon) can form compounds with highly electronegative elements like fluorine.
